claim: flow_plan.md's "changeset.json (output)" example (the retarget op literal, ~lines 249-258) orders a retarget op's keys op_id, type, spec_node_id, spec_hash, target, labels, deps, reason — target ahead of deps.
authoritative_source: arch_changeset_builder.md's "Canonical Output" section: "Field order inside every op is fixed (op_id, type, spec_node_kind, spec_node_id, spec_hash, idempotency, parent, deps, priority, title, body, target, labels, reason)" — one order for every op kind, deps ahead of target/labels, applied without exception.
evidence: One Op struct cannot emit both orders, so one of these leaves is wrong. flow_plan.md's own retarget example puts target before deps; arch_changeset_builder.md's "Canonical Output" section explicitly fixes a single field order across every op kind with deps ahead of target/labels/reason. arch_changeset_builder.md's own informal "Retarget op shape" table also lists target ahead of spec_node_id/spec_hash/labels/deps (a third, differently-ordered rendering, though that table reads as an enumeration of relevant fields rather than a serialization order — it likewise never applies to a create op, so it cannot itself be the canonical rule the file already states elsewhere). test_changeset_builder.md's "Canonical schema and field order" scenario adds a supporting inconsistency: it lists spec_node_id, idempotency, parent, deps, priority, title, body, target, labels, reason for the canonical assertion but omits spec_hash entirely, even though spec_hash is a create-op field too (arch_changeset_builder.md's Op Kinds / spec_node_kind tables) and appears in the Canonical Output field list. plan/types_test.go's TestOp_RetargetCanonicalFieldOrder follows arch_changeset_builder.md's explicit "Canonical Output" rule (deps before target) as the more authoritative of the conflicting statements — an explicit, general field-order rule against an illustrative example — but only the authoring loop can settle which leaf is wrong and correct the others to match.
proposed_fix: Pick one field order for the retarget op (deps-before-target, matching the general Canonical Output rule already used for creates and closes) and make flow_plan.md's example, arch_changeset_builder.md's Retarget op shape table, and test_changeset_builder.md's canonical-order scenario (adding spec_hash to its field list) agree with it and with each other.
